newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WEAKENED AUSTRALIAN BONDS CONTEMPLATE NEXT MOVE.
newsitem.headline: WEAKENED AUSTRALIAN BONDS CONTEMPLATE NEXT MOVE.

text.p: *Australian bond futures remained around the sharply lower levels seen during pre-weekend SYCOM trading as the market contemplated its next move
*U.S. Treasuries continue to weigh heavily on market
Australian bonds were marked down sharply at the opening on Monday in what many traders considered an overdone reaction to a bearish U.S. market.
"People are just trying to work out what to do next. There is no reason for us to be down here and the move in the U.S. looks grossly overdone," one trader said.

The local 10-year bond futures contract has shed around 25 basis points since Thursday's close as the weight of continued weakness in the U.S. soured local technicals, even though domestic fundamentals remain superior to those of the U.S.

The 10-year contract has sliced through a major support zone of 93.470 to 93.360, leaving it vulnerable to further downward pressure, although a break back above 93.310 could spark a 10 basis point rally, technical analysts said.

U.S. Treasuries fell sharply again on Friday as nervousness about the strength of the economy continued to grip the market ahead of a week of major U.S. data, particularly Wednesday's retail sales as a key guide to consumer demand.
Local data is fairly thin this week, although the market is keenly awaiting a speech by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane in Perth on Tuesday for clues on future monetary policy.

The local market underperformed against the dollar bloc, particularly against Canada which held its ground against the U.S. on Friday. The local yield curve also steepened sharply with the U.S. sell-off having a greater impact on the long end.
